title: Polish Superstitions: Thumbs, Thresholds and Carp Scales
excerpt: Polish superstitions by occasion: holding thumbs, Nie przez próg, carp scales on Wigilia, wedding months with an R and red ribbons on prams.
metaDescription: Polish superstitions by occasion: holding thumbs, Nie przez próg, carp scales on Wigilia, wedding months with an R and red ribbons on prams.
summary: In a 2018 CBOS survey, 54% of adult Poles believed in at least one common superstition, and 75% hold their thumbs (trzymać kciuki) for someone at least occasionally.
Everyday Polish superstitions include knocking on unpainted wood, never greeting across a threshold, and grabbing a button when you see a chimney sweep.
Polish Christmas superstitions cluster around Wigilia: a carp scale in the wallet, a man as the first guest, and animals said to speak at midnight.
Weddings traditionally fall in months with an 'r', students avoid haircuts before the matura, and red ribbons on prams guard babies against urok.

factNotes: Sitting before a journey ('przysiąść przed podróżą'): no Polish source found for the pre-journey version; CBOS and careersinpoland document sitting down when you RETURN home for a forgotten item, so the article covers that version only. Whistling indoors: no Polish source tying it to money (that link is Russian folklore); article hedges it as 'many families frown on it, explanations vary'. Rain on the wedding day: no Polish source; article says it is a belief shared by many cultures and not specifically Polish. Sitting at the corner of the table (won't marry) and other pregnancy taboos (fire, haircuts, buying baby things early) were left out as unsourced. Bouquet beliefs (drying, pearls) come from a florist blog, read via search excerpt only, and are attributed as such. The 2019 pregnancy-superstition study (166 expectant mothers, Dąbrowska-Wnuk) was read only via its repository abstract/search summary. 'Połamania nóg/pióra' and not saying dziękuję are from popular press (eska/SE) plus careersinpoland, not academic sources. Christmas Eve items are consistent with /blog/wigilia-polish-christmas-eve (hay straw length, extra place for unexpected guest or remembrance). Featured cat photo was taken in Istanbul; caption does not claim Poland.
